target_customer: Consumer packaged goods brands that lose money to retailer deductions (today); at founding, DTC brands paying Airbnb hosts to place products
problem: Today: CPG brands lose revenue to invalid retailer deductions and spend heavy manual labor on cash application. At founding: DTC brands wanted awareness and sampling, and Airbnb hosts wanted extra income.
business_model: Today: software for CPG back offices, priced to the revenue recovered. At founding: commission to hosts on sales driven from product placement in short term rentals.
product_category: AI back office automation for CPG retail operations (originally Airbnb product placement marketplace)

founders.name: Akash Raju
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch July 2020 name him CEO. Their campus pop-up shop work with brands inspired the first idea.

founders.name: Anuj Mehta
founders.role: COO at founding, now Co-Founder and CPO
founders.background_notes: Titled COO in TechCrunch July 2020 and CPO on the YC page.

founders.name: Kushal Negi
founders.background_notes: Named a co-founder by TechCrunch in 2020 and 2026 but not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: The 2020 product was a two sided marketplace with sample logistics and a digital lookbook for about 750 properties, which is ordinary web engineering. The later deductions agents are harder but that is after the pivot.

defensibility.rationale: Product placement in rentals had no stated proprietary supply, data or contracts beyond the host list, and traction fell when COVID cut travel. The founders later said they lacked product market fit.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent is named in 2020 coverage, which notes only that hotels already do product placement. The idea failed on its own and the team pivoted by 2024.

market_need_then: In 2020 DTC brands wanted cheap awareness and sampling and the founders saw it at campus pop-ups. About 750 properties joined by July 2020 with many booked through September, but launch landed just before COVID travel disruption.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, outcome focused copy such as 'We win back cash for CPG brands' with a named guarantee (company site).

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. The name is shared with at least one unrelated company (Panoplai was formerly Glimpse), and the company uses a try prefix domain.

pivots.from: Airbnb product placement marketplace for brands and hosts
pivots.to: AI deductions management and revenue recovery for CPG brands
pivots.why: CEO told TechCrunch they lacked product market fit and decided to hard pivot.

outcome_analysis: Glimpse launched an Airbnb product placement marketplace in March 2020 with about 750 properties, then lost momentum when COVID hit travel and, in the founders' words, never found product market fit. By 2024 it hard pivoted to AI agents that dispute invalid retailer deductions for CPG brands, raised a $10M round led by 8VC in April 2025 and a $35M Series A led by a16z in March 2026, and reports 200+ brand customers. The pivot, not the original idea, is the success story.
notes: The April 2025 round was called a Series A by the company and press at the time (natlawreview, pulse2) and relabeled seed by TechCrunch in 2026; recorded as seed with this caveat. TechCrunch states $52M raised to date including pre-pivot funding, which exceeds the two recorded rounds by about $7M; the pre-pivot round was not found. A podcast listing reportedly puts the total at about $17M after the 2025 round (unverified). A search snippet said the company was once called Dime, from a single unopened page, so it is not recorded as a rebrand. Competitor list is empty because 2020 coverage names none; TechCrunch 2026 names Revya and Confido but those post date the founding idea. Round Funded lists a different 'Glimpse' (video chat); ignored.
